'''Rosemary A. Roberts''' is a [[Statistics education|statistics educator]] who led the creation of the [[AP Statistics]] course and exam for US secondary school students,{{r|watkins}} and who later chaired the Statistical Education Section of the [[American Statistical Association]].{{r|ses}}
Educated in England and Canada, she spent many years working in the US before her 2013 retirement.{{r|profile|retire}}

Roberts earned a bachelor's degree in England, at the [[University of Reading]]. She completed her Ph.D. in statistics at the [[University of Waterloo]].{{r|profile}} Among her early works, she co-authored the [[Chang and Roberts algorithm]] in 1979.<ref>{{Citation|title=An improved algorithm for decentralized extrema-finding in circular configurations of processes|journal=Communications of the ACM|volume=22|issue=5|year=1979|pages=281&ndash;283|publisher=ACM|author=Ernest Chang; Rosemary Roberts|doi=10.1145/359104.359108|doi-access=free}}</ref> She joined the mathematics department at [[Bowdoin College]] in 1984, retired in 2013, and is now a [[professor emeritus]] there.{{r|retire}}

In 1987, with Tom Moore of [[Grinnell College]], she co-founded the Statistics in the Liberal Arts Workshop (SLAW), an annual meeting of statisticians at liberal arts colleges held every summer at Grinnell.{{r|slaw}}
With [[Ann E. Watkins]], Chris Olsen, and Richard Scheaffer,
She is the coauthor of ''The Teacher's Guide for AP Statistics'' (The College Board, 1997).{{r|peck}}

Roberts was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1997.{{r|fasa}}
